div.head: Northu 48
div.ab: Gif þonne æni man agiten wurðe, þæt ǽnigne hæðenscipe heonan forð dreoge oððe on blot oððe on firhte oððe on ænig wiccecræft lufige oððe idola wurðinge, gif he sy cynges þegn, gilde X healfmarc, healf Criste, healf þam cynge.

Gif þonne æni man agiten wurðe þæt ænigne hæðenscipe heonan forð dreoge oððe on blot oððe on firhte oððe on ænig wiccecræft lufige oððe idola wurðinge, gif he sy cynges þegn, gilde X healfmarc: healf Criste, healf þam cynge.

Wenn aber irgend jemand betroffen wird, dass er hinfort irgend ein Heidenwerk vornimmt, bestehend entweder in Opfer oder in Wahrsagung oder auf irgend eine [Weise] Zauberei pflegt oder Götzen-Verehrung [verehrt?], wenn er Königsthegn ist, zahle er 10 Halbmark, halb Christo [dem Bischofe], halb dem König.

But if anyone is found to practise any heathen act henceforth, whether in sacrifice or in divination, or loves witchcraft in any [way] or the worship of idols [worships?], if he is a king's thegn, let him pay 10 half-marks, half to Christ [the bishop], half to the king.

If, then, any man is discovered who henceforth carries on any heathen practice, either by sacrifice or divination, or practises witchcraft by any means, or worship of idols, he is to pay, if he is a king's thegn, 10 half-marks, half to Christ, half to the king.

Accordingly, if anyone comes to be discovered who henceforth practices any heathen rituals, either through sacrifice or through divination or through any form of witchcraft or the worship of idols, if he is the king’s thane, he is to pay ten half-marks: half to Christ, half to the king.

note.label: draws on
note.quote: Northu. 48 (below, n. 152) seems to draw on Cnut’s.

div.note: After ‘on ænig’ Liebermann suggests supplying ‘þing’, or reading ‘ænige wisan’ with II Cn 5.1. The second ‘oððe’ is written ‘ł’ in D. Cnut has ‘weorðige’ (so the editors translate); Toller reads ‘weorðunge’. Liebermann compares II Cn 5.1.; U: checked against Whitelock, EHD I (1979), and corrected (before: ‘If, then, any man is discovered who henceforth carries on any heathen practice, either by sacrifice or by divination, or practises witchcraft by any means, or worship of idols, he is to pay, if he is a king's thegn, 10 half-marks, half to Christ, half to the king.’).
